body.statement: For next-4-week unit demand sum forecasts from a pooled ridge model with lags 1-4 and 4/13-week rolling means (alpha=1.0, no log/trend/cat/promo/clip/window/series_mean, naive inverse transform), adding last year's demand over the same 4-week window as a feature (treatment: yoy=true) reduces relative WAPE by at least 1.0% (SESOI) versus the identical model without that feature (comparator: yoy=false), as estimated by a two-way (series x rolling-origin) bootstrap under Design B (32 rolling origins, weeks 110-234, 260-week history).
body.estimand: relative WAPE reduction, next-4-week sum, two-way bootstrap
body.kills_if: The two-way bootstrap distribution of relative WAPE reduction (treatment vs comparator) has its one-sided 97.5% lower confidence bound at or below 0%, or the point estimate falls below the 1.0% SESOI, at alpha=0.025 -- i.e. we fail to reject no-improvement or the improvement is not practically meaningful. Idea is also dropped if treatment's WAPE is worse (negative reduction) on the point estimate.
